text:
An official within the Department of the Interior has attempted to liken the algae in the Lincoln Memorial Reflection Pool to that of Iran's navy(Image: Getty Images)

An official within President Donald Trump's administration put out a statement on Thursday, seemingly comparing the renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflection Pool to the status of the Iranian military.

On X, the Department of the Interior attempted to provide an update on the algae that has formed in the basin. "The advanced nanobubbler technology very effectively killed the algae that has plagued every Lincoln Reflecting Pool reopening—most infamously Obama's reopening—since 1922," the post read.

"The Reflecting Pool water is crystal clear, and our National Park Service team is now vacuuming up the dead algae resting on the bottom of some parts of the Reflecting Pool—just like the destroyed Iranian Navy resting on the bottom of the Persian Gulf," the department added. "The vacuuming is the final maintenance step after refilling the pool, and it will be complete in a few days."

The department's press team claimed that all of the algae closest to the memorial of the 16th president "has been vacuumed up, and the beautiful American Flag Blue coating on the bottom of the pool can be seen clearly." The department then went on to lambast former President Barack Obama, who also attempted renovations on the reflection pool.

"Previous administrations—most notably under Obama—failed to maintain the Reflecting Pool, and after refilling the pool, the water would quickly become murky and thick with massive clumps of algae floating on the surface," the department added. "The photos below show how the nanobubbler technology and vacuuming have been incredibly effective, making the water crystal clear with the American Flag Blue coating shining brightly on the bottom of the pool."

Maintenance crews have been pouring hydrogen peroxide into the pool in order to clear the algae  (Image: Getty Images)

"As our National Park Service team noted, the Reflecting Pool is now so 'blue' that the Fake News Media, which has been staked out at the Reflecting Pool for weeks, has fled!" the Interior Department noted. The claims on X echo those of an Interior Department official who told the Irish Star that the algae "is dead."

"Versus previous administrations, the National Park Service is actually maintaining the beautifully completed Reflecting Pool," the official said. "The nanobubbler technology has successfully destroyed the algae bloom that has plagued every pool reopening since 1922, most infamously, the Obama pool reopening that resulted in massive algae clumps taking over the pool's surface following years of construction that cost taxpayers millions upon millions, only to be broken and disgusting days later."

According to an official within the department, the entire pool is now "crystal clear." (Image: Getty Images)

"Now, due to deploying the advanced nanobubbler technology, the algae is dead and being vacuumed up as we speak," they added. ""We thank President Trump for fixing the Reflecting Pool for good."

Despite their claims that the algae is gone and that the $14 million renovation is visible, reports have surfaced that sections of the paint are now coming off.

The claims on X echo those of an Interior Department official who told the Irish Star that the algae "is dead." (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The viral video of the chunk of blue paint also shows the extent of the algae that has grown in the pool since it was filled with water after the renovations were completed. Crews were seen inside the pool pouring hydrogen peroxide canisters to rid the body of water of the green algae.

A massive chunk of blue paint floated to the surface of the pool, ripped from the bottom. Trump’s remodeled Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, with its “American flag blue” bottom turned chartreuse from an algal bloom that park service workers struggled to address Tuesday, just days after it was refilled with water and reopened to the public.

A massive chunk of blue paint floated to the surface of the pool, ripped from the bottom. Trump’s remodeled Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool(Image: Getty Images)

Algae has been a common foe of the reflection pool since it opened more than 100 years ago, but Trump set his sights on addressing it as part of his aggressive push to beautify Washington ahead of the country's 250th anniversary. The project, which was announced by Trump in April, awarded a $14.8 million contract to the company that has since attempted to restore the pool.

According to the president, He was inspired by complaints from a friend visiting from Germany who called the pool dark and disgusting.
